extracted.intended_audience: educated English-speaking general readers and students/scholars of Japanese religion, culture, and sociology
extracted.subtask_description: A narrative-ethnographic chapter describing Nō theatre, the Nichiren sect, the Ikegami festival and monastery life, with observations on priestly education, popular religiosity, and institutional adaptation to modernity in early 20th-century Japan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nō drama as expression and cultivation of national aesthetic and ethical life
rubrics_metrics.description: Like the old Greek drama, but unlike anything which we have ... the Nō has both expressed and cultivated much of what has been artistically and ethically best of the life characteristic of the national development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nō should be evaluated not only for its formal artistic merits but for how it embodies and cultivates the aesthetic and ethical ideals of Japanese national life; compare its societal role to that of Greek drama rather than to contemporary popular entertainments.

rubrics_metrics.name: School-specific treatment of religious themes (handling of Bushidō)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ho-sho-kwai, or more 'militant' of the two schools, dealt with more discretion -- not to say timorousness -- with the religious value of the Bushidō, and with the future fate of those who, without the faith of Buddhism, are governed by its moral code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a Nō performance or school, note differences in emphasis and tact regarding religious doctrine and moral consequences: some schools treat the religious aspects of Bushidō more cautiously, affecting thematic presentation and moral messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Didactic moral severity and proportionality in dramatic justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Plays (e.g., 'Akogi') sometimes present apparently disproportionate punishments for relatively trivial or local transgressions (poaching, killing fish) and insist on absolute, unforgivable guilt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret such dramatic severity with cultural-historical context (compare to old game-laws or religious sanctions elsewhere) and beware of anachronistic foreign criticism; consider the didactic or ritual function rather than literal proportional justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of the written scripture in Nichiren identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal which it makes to the authority of the written word ... this scripture must not be contested or even questioned as to its right to demand submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core criterion for understanding/evaluating the Nichiren sect is its doctrinal reliance on a fixed authoritative scripture; this shapes institutional behavior, militancy, and intolerance of doctrinal dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militant-patriotic axiom linking religion and state welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: The one tenet ... was the assertion that 'the prosperity or decline of the state depends entirely upon the truth or perversion of its religion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments of the sect should account for its conviction that religious correctness is a matter of national fate; this axiom explains political activism, surveillance of members' fidelity, and patriotic appeal to military classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating popular religious festivals: mixture of devotion and commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: The wholly frank exposure of the mixture of motives which has brought the crowds together ... the crowd on the outside, for the most part, was not on religion bent ... 'going to see the religious procession and selling our cabbages.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not evaluate a sect solely by the commercialized or festive behaviors of crowds at public celebrations; distinguish between sincere devotional practice in the sanctum and the popular, mixed motives of festival-goers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy toward harmless superstitions (reform strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the superstitions connected with the celebration were not positively harmful, it was the policy of the reforming and progressive party of the sect to leave them to die away of themselves as the people at large became more enlightened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical reform within religious institutions should favor gradualism: allow non-harmful popular superstitions to fade with education rather than forcibly suppressing them, to avoid counterproductive backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priestly education should adapt to modern moral and intellectual needs
rubrics_metrics.description: My pupil ... had succeeded in founding a college for the young priests of the Nichiren sect in such manner as to fit them for usefulness under conditions belonging to the moral and religious development of the 'New Japan.' ... his life-work to be the moral reform and improved mental culture of the priesthood of his sect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate seminaries/colleges by how well they combine traditional religious instruction with modern curricula (literature, sciences), moral reform aims, and preparation for contemporary social roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive formation for temple boys: arms, music, and secular instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: As it was in ancient Greece, so it is now in Japan; arms and music must not be neglected in the preparation to serve his country of the modern Buddhist priest. Sword-dancing ... a duet performed upon a flute and a harp ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training programs for priests or temple students should be assessed for their holistic formation (physical/martial training, arts/music, and secular studies) alongside theological instruction, reflecting a civic as well as religious role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visible orderliness, attentiveness and decorum as indicators of sincere worship
rubrics_metrics.description: What had every appearance of serious and devout religious worship ... All were neatly dressed ... no evidences of having shuffled into unbrushed garments ... all responded to the sutras and intoned the appointed prayers ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging the quality of religious life or instruction, note observable discipline, decorum, and engaged participation in worship as proxies for sincerity and effective formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literacy and scholarship as measures of priestly influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the hundreds of Tâoist priests he had met, the vast majority could not even read the Chinese ideographs when he wrote them ... Among the Buddhist priests in China ... perhaps three or four in every ten could make some pretence of education; and there were even a very few who were real scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a religious tradition's potential for positive influence by the education and literacy of its clergy; higher levels of scholarship correlate with greater moral and social influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional hospitality and ceremonial presentation as markers of status and tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: The rooms had been especially decorated; and the finest of the lacquer trays and bowls and the best of the porcelain ... had been brought out of the store-house in honour of the occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ceremonial hospitality, preservation of treasures, and use of traditional ritual accoutrements signal institutional dignity, historical continuity, and claims to cultural authority — relevant when evaluating monastery prestige and social position.
